newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Veba plans U.S. expansion.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Veba plans U.S. expansion.

text.p: German diversified utility Veba AG said Tuesday it plans to spend 4.1 billion marks ($2.4 billion) in the next five years on expansion in North America, with the focus of the expansion on its Huels chemical unit.

A spokesman for Veba confirmed a report in Tuesday's Financial Times that cited Veba management board Chairman Ulrich Hartmann saying that Veba planned to expand in the region through acquisitions and internal growth.
Veba plans to list its shares on the New York Stock Exchange on Oct. 8.

Hartmann described the flotation as "one piece of the mosaic" of internationalization and said he hoped U.S. holdings would rise above 15 percent following the listing from their current level of 12.5 percent.
He reiterates what he had said previously about the group not needing to raise capital to finance its growth programme.

"I wouldn't rule out that we would raise capital in the future (if any big acquisition came along) but according to our current plans we can finance any acquisitions ourselves," Hartmann told the newspaper.

Veba aims to develop its phenals plant in Mobile, Ala. It also intends to grow its presence in the transportation of electronic systems and components, and in manufacturing wafers for computer chips, the report said.
Hartmann said he expected some minor acquisitions, but said chemicals acquisitions are overpriced in the U.S. market.
